Art & Culture.title: Knoll Reimagines Florence Knoll’s Storage System With Sam Chermayeff
Art & Culture.text: SummaryKnoll taps Sam Chermayeff to reimagine Florence Knoll’s 1961 credenzas.The storage collection introduces tall shelving, bar cabinets, and table drawers.Modern updates include striking Dark Python, Iris, and Dark Red Ultra lacquers.Knoll has introduced the Knoll Chermayeff Storage collection, a new furniture line designed by architect Sam Chermayeff that reimagines the brand's historic modernist principles for contemporary living. Serving as a direct evolution of Florence Knoll’s iconic 1961 credenzas, the collection honors the rigorous steel, veneer, and marble construction logic of the original pieces while introducing entirely new forms and proportions. The collection falls into a category described by Knoll Creative Director Jonathan Olivares as "adaptive reuse," extending classic architectural visions to encourage more fluid ways of living and working.The resulting pieces shift storage from a purely practical necessity into an architectural backdrop for books, objects and personal artifacts. Tall open shelving extends the system vertically, creating a stronger spatial presence while also offering opportunities to subtly divide a room, while a dedicated bar cabinet turns storage into a focal point for entertaining.Coffee, side and console tables broaden the collection further, incorporating concealed drawers that bring everyday organization into lower, more informal furniture typologies. Visually, the pieces retain the clean geometry and rigor associated with Florence Knoll’s original credenzas, but Chermayeff introduces a more expressive character through altered proportions and a newly energized palette, including Dark Red Ultra, Dark Python and Iris lacquer finishes.That balance between historical continuity and contemporary flexibility separates Chermayeff Storage from a conventional Knoll reissue. Where restorations typically preserve an existing object through updated materials, finishes or colors, Chermayeff treats Florence Knoll’s original system more like an architectural vocabulary that can be expanded and rearranged according to how people now live, work and gather.The approach also aligns with Chermayeff’s broader interest in communal living, allowing storage to function as infrastructure for shared spaces while retaining the refinement of the 1961 designs. Knoll Chermayeff Storage is available to purchase through Knoll, bringing the brand’s mid-century foundations into a more adaptable family of furniture for contemporary residential and workplace settings.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Art & Culture.title: From Day One to the Present: NITRO MICROPHONE UNDERGROUND
Art & Culture.text: The Roots of AuthenticityJapanese hip-hop’s early history was anchored in Tokyo, where a generation captivated by rap’s refined style watched as the genre entered its first domestic boom. By the mid-1990s, tracks like “DA.YO.NE” pushed hip-hop into the mainstream, but beneath the surface, a divide emerged between commercial "pop" rap and the underground. While the media turned "check it out" into a meme, the underground scene rejected commercialism, with artists quietly sharpening their skills through intense competition.The genba (frontline) of this movement was Shibuya’s Club CAVE, where the event “A BAOA QU” became a sanctuary for individuals who shared a "fly" conviction – a space where figures from music and fashion searched for like-minded peers. Here, the blueprint for NITRO MICROPHONE UNDERGROUND (NMU) began to form through organic connections rather than a calculated plan to start a group.Formation and the "Reality" of the SceneThe future members were already fixtures in the Shibuya and Harajuku scenes: MACKA-CHIN and XBS were high school classmates; GORE-TEX and S-WORD worked in Shibuya; while SUIKEN and DABO ran events in Nishi-Azabu. Their bond deepened naturally through the shops and clubs they frequented. When they were offered a monthly residency at CAVE, the parties quickly became legendary.In an era when recording equipment was scarce, rappers typically performed original lyrics over imported US 12-inch instrumentals — a practice in which one’s taste was judged by their choice of beat. As these vibrant parties drew staff from iconic record shops like Manhattan Records and CISCO, a collective of roughly 30 people solidified under the loose banner of "about NITRO MICROPHONE UNDERGROUND." This momentum caught the eye of Kazuteru Maekawa of Lexington Co., Ltd., who proposed a collaboration. Despite a lingering aversion to "selling out," those who remained committed - while others left for conventional jobs - formed the core of NMU.The Shibuya Udagawa SpiritThe 1999 release of “REQUIEM” - a four-man mic relay featuring MACKA-CHIN, S-WORD, GORE-TEX and an uncredited SUIKEN - helped position Udagawacho as a global epicenter of culture. The area was defined by an intimidating atmosphere created by "unapologetically arrogant" record and clothing store staff. This environment acted as a "meaningful barrier" that forced young fans to become hungrier and more discerning – a sensibility that NMU embodied as the first group to truly emerge from that specific terrain.The group name itself was a mix of spontaneity and radio-controlled car culture, with "Nitro" referencing nitroglycerin and "Microphone" paying homage to MICROPHONE PAGER. Under Maekawa’s guidance, what was once a catchphrase in artwork became the official group name to promote their first CD, Nitro Works.Major Success and the Def Jam EraNMU redefined Tokyo hip-hop by focusing on a localized reality: the inside jokes and mischief of the Harajuku-Shibuya radius. In 2000, they released their signature classic, "NITRO MICROPHONE UNDERGROUND," featuring all eight members. BIGZAM’s iconic lyric, “Shibuya Udagawa-hatsu” (“Shibuya Udagawa-born”), became the group's definitive slogan.Their self-titled debut album was an explosive success. Initially released as a limited 20,000-unit pressing via Reality Records, it sold out instantly. This served as a springboard for a major deal with Def Jam Japan, making NMU the first release in the label’s domestic catalog. While the move to a major label provided massive exposure in magazines like WOOFIN’ and Fine, the transition was not without friction regarding creative control and financial returns.In response, the members took control of their business interests by launching Night Rich Co., Ltd. and the apparel brand NITROW. The repackaged major album eventually sold over 150,000 copies, propelling the members into successful solo careers at major labels like Sony and Victor. This era marked the transition of NMU from a loose underground collective into a multifaceted cultural operation.In the early 2000s, "selling out" was a term of hostility aimed at artists who lost creative control upon signing to a major label. NMU, however, managed to erase this stigma. Their stance was uncompromising: if they couldn't maintain creative control, they wouldn't sign. By choosing major-label staff they could trust, they proved that financial success didn't require sacrificing the integrity of their music.Breaking the Mold of Japanese RapThe same year that NMU released their self-titled debut, they swept the annual awards of blast magazine (Japan’s premier hip-hop publication), winning both Best Group and Best Album. At the time, the magazine did not distinguish between domestic and international acts, choosing instead the year’s most symbolic artists. NMU notably claimed the top spot over global heavyweights like Wu-Tang Clan, OutKast and De La Soul.While these accolades suggested a fully formed scene, the era was actually one of significant trial and error. Skepticism toward Japanese-language rap remained deeply rooted, and critics often dismissed NMU as mere Wu-Tang imitators. However, the group’s arrival was groundbreaking; their production quality stood shoulder-to-shoulder with US mainstream releases, effectively overturning the mindset of those who refused to acknowledge the legitimacy of Japanese rap.A Rare Major-Label Clean SweepNMU’s sensational presence was best exemplified by a rare feat: eventually, all eight members signed solo contracts with major labels. This was not merely due to the group’s commercial momentum, but the result of solo groundwork each member had laid prior to their collective breakthrough.Following the impact of their Def Jam Japan debut, SUIKEN was the first to charge into the major arena with Sony in 2001, followed closely by DABO and S-WORD. These solo ventures allowed members to move beyond ‘90s boom-bap, embracing a modern sonic landscape that included Neptunes-esque grooves and avant-garde experiments. MACKA-CHIN noted that the major-label environment provided high-tier studios and the resources to obsess over every detail, allowing them to maintain an uncompromising work ethic.Bridging the Gap and Expanding the EmpireBeyond solo albums, the members strengthened their individual names through high-profile collaborations. They bridged the subtle distance between domestic hip-hop and the rising R&B scene, featuring on tracks by artists like bird, wyolica and Namie Amuro.The collective’s reach expanded further through side projects like MABO (MACKA-CHIN and DABO) and AQUARIUS (DELI and YAKKO). By 2003, while GORE-TEX and BIGZAM were the only members yet to release solo records, the group’s influence remained untouchable. Simultaneously, XBS was busy co-founding the apparel brand nitrow, further cementing Nitro's status as a multifaceted cultural powerhouse.The Birth of nitrow and the Independent SpiritAt the turn of the 21st century, Shibuya’s Udagawacho had a distinct "reflexive uniform." In summer, the streets were filled with Tommy Hilfiger, Ralph Lauren and Nautica; in winter, they were camouflaged by The North Face and First Down jackets. Paired with Timberland boots, Air Force 1s and the essential durag or chew stick, this attire was a cultural rite of passage. NMU was the ultimate embodiment of this aesthetic, having filtered its sensibilities through the fashion hubs of Harajuku and Ueno.Beyond music, the group operated like an "independent nation" through their apparel brand, nitrow (later nitraid). Unlike artists who simply licensed their names, they controlled production and distribution themselves. This led to a historic, deep collaborative relationship with Nike that produced exclusive, members-only sneakers.The Nike Era: A Global Synergy    Under XBS’s leadership, nitraid achieved what was then unthinkable for a Japanese independent brand: a deep, collaborative relationship with Nike. This wasn't a standard endorsement; it resulted in several exclusive sneakers, including members-only "Staff" editions and retail versions of the Air Force 1 and Delta Force. Their influence extended to global giants like Stüssy, New Era and Levi’s® Fenom. At its peak, nitraid was a cultural powerhouse, blending high-end craftsmanship with a raw, "fly" street sensibility that predated the modern era of rapper-led fashion empires by nearly two decades.     End of an Era and the Road to HiatusIn early 2011, NMU released THE LABORATORY, an ambitious project designed to evolve their sound through outside producers. However, the Great East Japan Earthquake struck just two months later, halting the country’s entertainment industry and making the group's planned nationwide NITRO CAMP tour impossible. MACKA-CHIN recalls that the disaster shifted national priorities toward survival rather than fashion or music.On another note, nitraid’s success was built on an uncompromising - and expensive - vision. Their seasonal exhibitions were legendary, featuring elaborate sets like a full-scale skate park inside a club. However, this commitment to "the ultimate experience" became a financial burden. The aftermath of the 2008 global financial crisis and the 2011 Tohoku earthquake added to the brand’s severe strain.Combined with internal financial disputes and the fact that each member was branching out into their own "family trees," NMU effectively entered a period of inactivity starting in 2012. A year later, nitraid also declared bankruptcy in 2013 with debts totaling ¥250 million JPY. XBS reflects on this period not with regret, but as a rare, valuable life experience that few in the industry ever encountered.Solo Ventures, Tokyo 25-ji and New ChallengesDuring the seven-year hiatus, the members respected an unspoken rule of creative freedom, never interfering in each other's solo pursuits. A notable milestone during this period was Tokyo 25-ji, a unit featuring DABO, MACKA-CHIN, SUIKEN and S-WORD. Overseen by DJ HAZIME and featuring legendary producers like MURO and DJ WATARAI, the project marked a dramatic reunion with their former home, Manhattan Records. DABO noted that this era allowed them to move beyond youthful bravado and imbue their purest emotions into lyrics about life and death.The hiatus also saw the members embrace diverse new roles. In 2014, DELI successfully ran for the Matsudo City Council, using his platform to address social issues like anti-nuclear activism; he is currently serving his third term. MACKA-CHIN explored ambient music and DJ compilations, while DABO launched the label Feel No Pain. XBS pursued photography under his real name, Nobuhiro Fukami, and served as creative director for basketball media like FLY. Meanwhile, GORE-TEX launched the apparel brand raidback® fabric and BIGZAM pursued acting under his real name, Hiroyuki Shintani.Reunion, Rebirth and the Vision for 2026In 2019, all eight members reunited for their 20th anniversary, heralded by the track "LIVE19" — a homage to their debut "LIVE99". Following a sold-out reunion show, S-WORD stepped away to focus on solo work, leaving NMU as a seven-member unit. Embracing a "natural, relaxed mindset," the group began collaborating with younger creators and producers like Numb and PART2STYLE, releasing the album SE7EN in 2022.NMU’s enduring influence was vividly displayed in 2024 when the group BAD HOP sampled them for the "8BALL CYPHER," bridging the gap between Udagawacho and a new generation. Now in 2026, the group remains prolific, releasing singles like “SHUTTA,” “Day One,” “Black Moon”, “G.U.I.” and “Eclipse” as they prepare for their sixth album.MACKA-CHIN reflects that while they are often viewed as legends, their ultimate goal remains to break out and truly become musicians. As Utamaru (RHYMESTER) observes, NMU remains the iconic presence of Tokyo hip-hop — an "invincible fleet" that continues to kill it decades later.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

At its center is an original heart motif and collaborative logo designed by VERDY, whose work across Girls Don't Cry and Wasted Youth has made him a recognizable figure in global streetwear. The graphics are applied across familiar silhouettes, balancing ER's youthful aesthetic with VERDY's bold, characterful approach to design.The ER x VERDY collection launches October 24, 2026, through BEAUTY&YOUTH UNITED ARROWS' Shinjuku Women's Store and Osaka store, as well as the United Arrows online store. Entertainment.title: Alpha Industries Just Blacked Out the MA-1, B-15 and CWU-45 for Its “Triple Black Pack”
Entertainment.text: SummaryAlpha Industries applies sneaker culture’s “triple black” formula to three of its most recognizable flight jacketsShell, lining and branding tag all go black, removing the contrast linings long tied to the label’s outerwearA campaign set inside a fictional design lab follows the jackets from raw material to finished garment to wearerAlpha Industries has unveiled the Triple Black Pack for FW26, reworking the MA-1 Heritage, B-15 Intermediate Flight Jacket and CWU-45 Heritage in black from the outer shell through to the lining and tag. The result is a trio of the brand’s core flight jackets stripped of every contrasting element.The concept comes from footwear. In sneaker circles, “triple black” describes a shoe where the upper, midsole and outsole all share the same black finish. Alpha Industries maps that three-part formula directly onto its jackets, with the shell, the lining and the tag standing in for those three zones.The lining is where the change lands hardest. Contrast linings have been a defining feature of Alpha’s flight jackets for decades, none more recognizable than the bright orange inside the MA-1. Here, that pop of color is gone entirely. With black running through every layer, the jackets now present a single, unbroken tone, so the look stays consistent whether the zip is done up or the front hangs open.The silhouettes themselves remain familiar. The MA-1 Heritage, B-15 Intermediate Flight Jacket and CWU-45 Heritage each keep the shapes Alpha fans already know, with the all-black treatment serving as the sole transformation. That restraint keeps the focus on color as the design statement, letting the blacked-out finish do the work.The Alpha Industries Triple Black Pack is available now online, at selected retailers and the Alpha Industries Store in Frankfurt am Main.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: Thierry Henry Gives a Closer Look at On's Debut Football Boot
Entertainment.text: SummaryOn Director of Football Thierry Henry shared a closer look at the brand's debut football boot on InstagramThe prototype features On's LightSpray technology for a seamless translucent upperThe boot is set for a public release in early 2027 with Kylian Mbappé leading the athlete rosterOn and Director of Football Thierry Henry have offered a closer look at the Swiss brand's debut On Football Boot. Shared via Instagram, the prototype reveals the technical foundation and design direction behind On's entry into the football footwear market. The cleat was initially first worn by Kylian Mbappé.Stamped with the development code ON-DCPT-KM210, the prototype introduces a thin, translucent upper constructed using On’s proprietary LightSpray technology. The robotic spraying process eliminates traditional seams and structural overlays, giving the silhouette a stripped-back appearance focused on performance and weight reduction.The preview follows On’s formal expansion into football, featuring an athlete roster led by Real Madrid star Kylian Mbappé and Barcelona midfielder Sydney Schertenleib. While Henry's teaser showcases a development prototype, it highlights how the Swiss performance label plans to bring its footwear engineering directly to the pitch.The On football boot is scheduled to launch to the public in early 2027.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Following the box-office success of the 2024 Mobile Suit Gundam SEED FREEDOM movie, Bandai Namco Filmworks has confirmed that the highly anticipated prequel will make its theatrical debut in Japan on January 15, 2027, followed by a North American theatrical rollout in February 2027.Directed by Mitsuo Fukuda, the project holds deep historical significance for the franchise, as its core scenario and initial storyboards were originally developed two decades ago as a planned OVA by the late lead writer Chiaki Morosawa. Entertainment.title: ‘Ghost of Tsushima: Legends’ Anime Delayed to 2028
Entertainment.text: SummaryGhost of Tsushima: Legends anime is delayed to 2028, confirmed at NYCC 2026.Mayumi Sako and Shinya Fukumatsu join the adaptation's voice cast.Additional staff members will ensure the series maintains the game's authentic aesthetic.Ghost of Tsushima: Legends will arrive later than originally planned, with Crunchyroll confirming that the anime adaptation has been pushed from its previously announced 2027 window to 2028. The updated timing was revealed during Crunchyroll’s New York Comic Con 2026 panel, where attendees were also shown an exclusive work-in-progress preview of the series; no reason for the delay has been given.Alongside the revised release window, Mayumi Saco and Shinya Fukumatsu were announced as part of the Japanese voice cast in currently undisclosed roles. Saco notably voiced Tomoe in the original Ghost of Tsushima game, while Fukumatsu is known for roles including Bomb in One-Punch Man. The series will stream exclusively on Crunchyroll when it premieres in 2028.First announced at CES 2025, the anime adapts Ghost of Tsushima: Legends, the supernatural cooperative multiplayer mode introduced to Sucker Punch Productions’ 2020 action-adventure game, rather than directly retelling Jin Sakai’s main campaign. Takanobu Mizuno, who directed Star Wars: Visions short “The Duel,” remains at the helm at Kamikaze Douga, with Gen Urobuchi overseeing series composition and co-writing the screenplay with Renji Oki, while Afro Samurai creator Takashi Okazaki handles character design.Newly confirmed staff include Keiji Inai as composer, Yoshikazu Iwanami as sound director, Yasumasa Koyama on sound effects and calligrapher Gyousyou Suzuki on the title treatment. The anime is produced by HAYATE in collaboration with Aniplex and PlayStation Productions, with Sony Music serving as its music and soundtrack partner, positioning the project as one of the most prominent crossovers between PlayStation’s gaming catalog and Sony’s expanding anime operations.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: Anthony Vaccarello Exits Saint Laurent After a Decade at the Helm
Entertainment.text: SummaryAnthony Vaccarello is officially exiting Saint Laurent after 10 years as Creative DirectorThe Belgian designer transformed the French house into a high-glamour powerhouse with sales peaking at 3.3 billion eurosParent company Kering announced it will reveal new creative leadership for the brand soonSaint Laurent and parent company Kering have officially confirmed the departure of Creative Director Anthony Vaccarello after a decade leading the house. The Belgian designer's dramatic September runway presentation in Paris served as his final collection for the luxury brand.Vaccarello took the creative reins in 2016 following Hedi Slimane, establishing a distinct visual language anchored in high-octane glamour, sharp tailoring, and sensual eveningwear presented against the backdrop of the Eiffel Tower. During his ten-year tenure, Saint Laurent’s annual revenues nearly tripled to a peak of €3.3 billion EUR, driven by popular everyday leather goods, sharp footwear, and statement outerwear alongside runway showpieces. Beyond fashion, Vaccarello expanded the brand’s cultural influence in 2023 with the launch of Saint Laurent Productions, backing films by directors including Pedro Almodóvar and David Cronenberg. On Vaccarello's departure, Luca de Meo, CEO of Kering said, "I would like to express my sincere gratitude to Anthony for his contribution to Saint Laurent over the past 10 years. Through his creative vision and exacting standards, he has contributed to strengthening the enduring influence of one of France's greatest couture houses, as we embark on a new chapter in its history."His exit comes as Kering undergoes a broader strategic turnaround under new Chief Executive Luca De Meo and Saint Laurent CEO Cédric Charbit. Moving forward, the house aims to reassert its authority beyond eveningwear by reinforcing its daywear, menswear, and high-end leather goods offerings.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast
